subject: chemistry
title: Chemical Bonding & Structure Adventure 1: Ionic and covalent bonding
welcome_lead: Today you'll lose, share or pool electrons — ionic, covalent and metallic bonds.
meta_desc: Chemistry — ionic, covalent (polar and non-polar), metallic bonding, properties.
final_note: You learned ionic = transfer giving lattice, covalent = shared pair (polar if electronegativity differs), metallic = sea of delocalised e⁻.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Metal + non-metal: electrons transfer.

Na (1 valence e⁻) loses → Na⁺; Cl (7 valence e⁻) gains → Cl⁻. Lattice held by electrostatic attraction.

Properties: high mp, conduct when molten or aqueous, brittle, often soluble in water.

Non-metal + non-metal: electrons shared.

H₂, Cl₂, CO₂, H₂O.

Polarity: if ΔEN > 0, bond is polar. C-O is polar (δ⁺C-Oδ⁻).
Molecule is polar if dipoles don't cancel. CO₂ linear → non-polar; H₂O bent → polar.

Metal cations sit in a sea of delocalised electrons.

Explains:
- Electrical conductivity (e⁻ free to move).
- Malleability (cations slide past one another).
- High mp (strong attraction).

Bond strength: charge density (Mg²⁺ > Na⁺), explaining mp Mg > Na.

What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.

mcqs.q: What state are the ions in when defining lattice enthalpy of formation?
options: Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
Gaseous ions — lattice enthalpy is the energy change when one mole of solid ionic compound forms from its constituent ions in the GAS phase.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
The ions are in aqueous solution before forming the lattice.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
